memos.risk:
Risk officer call: refuse. Don't buy at any size.

Refusal triggers, all present in the brief:
- Class is OPERATOR, but the launch is near-total concentration: bundle_share and top3_share at 1.0, top-5 buyers hold 99.4% of early buys, and 1,008 SOL came from ~21 buyers in the first two minutes with a launch bot present. This is the pattern that breaks the "break-even" operator base rate; the operator's exit liquidity is the desk.
- Sell-to-buy ratio of 0.0008 at the two-minute mark means almost nothing could sell into the launch.
- The 194x return from 30 minutes ago with the name "American Trust Fund System" (a trust-and-fund name used in fake-authority tricks) adds no reason for confidence.

The 1,190 SOL pool gives some depth, but a $20 ticket's 1.4-5.1% round trip cost is trivial next to a concentrated holder base that can dump in one block. Skip.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying ATFS now is thin, and the brief mostly argues against it.

The one real signal is demand that persisted after graduation: 151 buyers and 66 SOL bought over the last 15 minutes against 15 sellers and 15 SOL sold, a net inflow of about 51 SOL and a 9% return in that window. Sell-to-buy ratio at 0.0008 means almost nobody sold in the first two minutes.

But the same data reads as a bundled operator launch. Over 1,000 SOL was bought in the first two minutes by 21 buyers, the top five took 99% of early buys, a launch bot was present, and the curve shows bundle share at 1.0. A 2.9x "completer share" and a 195% 30-minute gain also fit a coin that was pumped to graduation by its own insiders. Operator-backed coins have roughly broken even, and nothing here shows the early holders have exited, so the last 15 minutes of buying could be the exit liquidity being sold into. With a 30-second execution lag and 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs, a dip is likely to be hard to catch cleanly.

Verdict: no strong case for buying. Skip unless you have a specific reason to think the operator's distribution is finished.
memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss: insider distribution after a pump. The 2-minute graduation window shows 1,008.85 SOL bought by 21 buyers, with a top-5 buyer share of 99.4% and a launch bot present. That is one operator's accumulation, not organic demand. Operator coins have been roughly break-even, but this one is already up 195% in 30 minutes with a 9.5M USD market cap, so the operator holds a large unrealized gain and has every incentive to exit into any retail inflow. The curve shows top3_share 1.0 and bundle_share 1.0, so the supply sits with a handful of wallets.

Last 15 minutes: 66 SOL bought against 15.2 SOL sold, a 50.9 SOL net inflow. Recent buying is the exit liquidity. Drawdown from the 30-minute high is 0.0, which means no pullback has yet tested the level. A 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost will eat any small bounce. Skip.
